punchline: After three days of Tetris, people saw falling blocks even with their eyes closed, and Achor says our jobs train us the same way.
thirty_sec: At Harvard Medical School, 27 people played Tetris for hours a day, three days running. Afterwards some dreamed of falling shapes, and some saw the whole world as blocks to fit together. Shawn Achor calls it the Tetris Effect: the brain keeps hunting for whatever pattern it has practised. Spend all day looking for errors and you'll find them everywhere. His fix is to write down three good things a day. People who did it for a week were still happier six months later.
